{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c5fa53ca7e9f5e024f4a02eea94c6bf3ac6ceeecd87cf10332c70f8917e541eb","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:24","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Signal and marking confusables: steady versus flashing lights, lights versus arrows, white versus yellow lines and special-lane look-alikes","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: steady versus flashing red and yellow, solid lights versus arrows, white versus yellow lines, solid versus dashed lines, and shared center, reversible, reserved and flex lanes","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: steady versus flashing red and yellow, solid lights versus arrows, white versus yellow lines, solid versus dashed lines, and shared center, reversible, reserved and flex lanes
Confusable pairs among signals, pavement lines and special lanes, where steady and flashing versions or look-alike markings call for different actions; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Both a steady red and a flashing red require a full stop, but after a flashing red you may go once it is safe, while after a steady red you wait for green. [A01]
Why it matters: group red signals; confusable steady versus flashing red.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green, while a flashing red arrow means stop and then go when safe. [A01]
Why it matters: group red arrows; confusable steady versus flashing arrow.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Right turns on red are allowed whenever safe and not forbidden by a sign, but left turns on red only from a one-way street onto a one-way street. [A01]
Why it matters: group turning on red; confusable right on red versus left on red.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
A traffic light that is out or malfunctioning is handled like a stop sign, not like a yield sign or a green light. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; misconception a dark signal means go.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow means stop before the intersection if you have not entered it, while a flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution. [A02]
Why it matters: group yellow signals; confusable steady versus flashing yellow.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow arrow warns the arrow is about to turn red, while a flashing yellow arrow lets you turn after yielding. [A02]
Why it matters: group yellow arrows; confusable steady versus flashing arrow.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A02
On a steady green ball a left turn must yield to oncoming traffic, while under a green arrow no oncoming or crossing traffic should be moving. [A02]
Why it matters: group green signals; confusable green ball versus green arrow.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A02
Even on a green arrow you still watch for pedestrians, and even on a steady green you still yield to emergency vehicles. [A02]
Why it matters: group green signals; misconception green means no yielding at all.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A03
White lines separate lanes going the same way, while the yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way. [A03]
Why it matters: group line colors; confusable white versus yellow.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A03
A white dashed line may be crossed when safe, while a solid white line between lanes may be crossed only for a hazard or a turn within the next block. [A03]
Why it matters: group white lines; confusable dashed versus solid white.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A04
A single dashed yellow line allows passing when safe, while two solid yellow lines forbid passing from either side. [A04]
Why it matters: group yellow lines; confusable dashed versus double solid yellow.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A04
With a dashed line beside a solid yellow line, the line nearest you decides: dashed on your side allows passing, solid on your side does not. [A04]
Why it matters: group yellow lines; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A04
The double yellow exceptions are turning into a driveway and passing a vehicle going under half the speed limit, and the second never applies to farm equipment. [A04]
Why it matters: group yellow lines; misconception slow farm equipment may be passed on a double yellow.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A05
A shared center lane is marked with solid and dashed yellow lines and is used only for left turns and U-turns, while a reversible lane is marked with double dashed yellow lines and has different operating hours for each lane. [A05]
Why it matters: group special lanes; confusable shared center versus reversible.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A06
A reserved lane may be entered by other vehicles only to turn across it within the next half of a block. [A06]
Why it matters: group reserved lanes; confusable half block versus next block.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A07
A flex lane is the paved shoulder opened by signs as a travel lane, but large trucks may never use it even when its green arrow is lit. [A07]
Why it matters: group special lanes; misconception any vehicle may use an open flex lane.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A07
In a flex lane a yellow X means the lane is closing so you merge into the general-purpose lanes, while a red X means it is already closed. [A07]
Why it matters: group lane lights; confusable yellow X versus red X.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0042]
